about: Two parts. 'lookup': how a tool finds another program it starts (sf-mod-check, 7z, taskkill, the Papyrus compiler). 'spellings': pairs of path spellings a tool compares (a saved game folder against the one in use, an output folder against a folder it cleans). 'policy': where a path came from decides whether the tool may open it.
lookup_setup: Each case runs in a new empty temporary folder T, with the current folder set to T/cwd. 'cwd_files' are made in T/cwd. 'path' is the PATH list, in order: {"dir": "bin1", "files": [...]} is the full path of T/bin1, made with those files; {"dir": "Program Files/bin2", "quoted": true} is that full path in double quotes; {"entry": "."} and {"entry": ""} are written into PATH as they are; {"relative": "relbin"} writes the relative name relbin into PATH (T/cwd/relbin is made with 'files'). The file name $PROG means the program as the platform names it: tool.exe on Windows, tool (marked executable) elsewhere. 'query' is the name the tool asks for; $PROG there means tool on every platform. 'expect': {"found": "<dir>"} means the program in that PATH folder, {"found": null} means not found (the tool then says it is missing, naming the program, and never starts anything), {"given": "<path>"} means the path the user gave, used as given.

lookup.why: The control: a program on PATH is found.
A same-named program planted in the current folder must not win over PATH.
round3: sf-load-order C3 (shutil.which found a planted sf-mod-check.exe or 7z.exe in the current folder)

lookup.why: With the program only in the current folder, it is not found.
A . entry in PATH means the current folder: never searched.
An empty PATH entry also means the current folder.
A relative PATH entry depends on the current folder: never searched.
A quoted PATH entry with a space is normal on Windows.
The first PATH folder that holds the program wins.
A name that already has a PATHEXT extension is tried as it is.
A path with a folder part is the user's choice: used as given, never searched on PATH.
A Windows system program is started by its full path under %SystemRoot%\System32, never by PATH or the current folder.
round3: sf-load-order C3 (taskkill was found the same way)
StarfieldVoiceTool C2 (a saved game path with a trailing \ never matched, so the index rebuilt on every play)
sf-patch-day R1 (two case spellings of one folder on Linux)
sf-patch-day C6 (a substring test on xboxgames)

spellings.note: A folder counts as inside itself, so an output folder equal to a cleaned folder is refused too.

case_twins.why: Two folders whose names differ only in case: name both and say which one is used, never pick one silently.

policy.why: A network path the user typed is the user's choice.

policy.source: a file the tool reads (a plan, a manifest, a cache, an MCP request)
policy.why: A network path read from a file is not opened without the user's say: refuse it, or warn and skip it, naming the file it came from.
round3: sf-test-plan S1 (a plan's UNC zip: path opened an SMB share)
sf-papyrus-ref S1 (an MCP client can name a UNC path)
